_comment: Shared TS<->Rust signer for WHICH runtimes the product offers (#task:2195, root ops).
The product decision has two halves, and they are compared differently on purpose:
offered        — the create/profile picker list, ORDER-SENSITIVE. TS derives it as
RUNTIME_ORDER filtered by the selectable flag; Rust derives it as
backend-core `SELECTABLE_RUNTIMES`. Both must equal this sequence.
vocabularyOnly — kinds a row may hold that the product does not offer, compared as a
SORTED SET. Display order is a TS-only fact (RUNTIME_ORDER); Rust's
`RuntimeKind::ALL` is the closed vocabulary in its own order, so
asserting an order here would pin something neither side owns.
Neither side hand-writes these names in a test: each derives its answer from its own
authority and is held to this artifact, so a runtime offered on one side only — or
reordered in the picker on one side only — fails on both.
